messages.subject: Non-parametric "random effects"?
messages.body_plain:
Hello,

I've got a Bayesian model that takes days and days to run via MCMC, so I'm hoping maybe INLA can help make it more tractable. After going through the examples I can find that the individual pieces I need are all present, but I'm unsure of how to combine them in the appropriate way.

The data I'm trying to fit is hierarchical and multidimensional. Countries nested within regions nested within the globe, and then counts within countries that vary over time and age.

The simplest version of my model to give reasonable results with MCMC looks like this: I have a model with linear predictors (i.e. fixed effects on covariates specific to each country-year), a global non-parametric trend over time (e.g. random walk or GMRF), and finally region-specific non-parametric time trends. That last portion is sort of like a random effect, except that instead of offsets it's a set of non-parametric functions over time; the idea is to capture ways in which regional time trends differ from the global pattern.

Using INLA to fit the first two portions (linear predictors + global time trend) is easy. But I'm not sure how to specify that certain non-parametric functions only contribute to the predictions of certain observations, as in the region-specific trends. Can the control.predictor specification be used for this, or is there another way of specifying?

Thanks for any help. INLA looks great from what I've used so far!
Kyle

messages.body_plain:
Actually, I think that NA may be exactly what I want. When I first saw "random effect k" I interpreted it as specifically meaning "iid random variable k" and didn't realize it could be one of the many different models listed. I'm going to give it a shot now and report back on how it works. Thanks so much!

And sorry for not doing this the first time around, here's roughly how the model would look written out:

y_i,j ~ 1 + x_i,j + f_1(time_i,j, model="rw1") + f_j(time_i,j, model="rw1")

where j = 1, ...., n    (n = # regions)

messages.body_plain: The multithreading in INLA is really impressive - it just works. I'm tempted to build from source to see if I can get some additional speedups for my mammoth model, but I'm not sure if I should build against multithreaded ATLAS libraries or not. INLA seems to be using the available resources about as efficiently as possible (staying solidly in the 900-1150% CPU usage range when I give it 12 cores), so I'm wondering if it's best not to upset the balance...

messages.body_plain:
that is way beyond what inla is supposed to handle, and why inla stop when you have more than 38 thetas (which is the current upper limit in the table of designs used for the ccd integration).

do you really need all the the thetas?  can you group them, saying some of the rw1 has the same precision (you do this using the option 'replicate' see

http://www.r-inla.org/models/tools

alternative, is also to turn off the numerical integration of the hyperparameters, using

inla(..., control.inla = list(int.strategy = "eb"))

H

I think you may want the random effects in each of the 21 regions to
have the same precision, which you can write as

	f(year, model ="rw1", replicate = region)

where region \in 1.... nregion.

this extention is explained in

http://www.r-inla.org/models/tools

same for age.

Now that I've seen a use case I understand that they're extraordinarily useful.
